mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 4.25% in a given month reduces near-term discount rates, lowering the present value of expected equity cash flows and thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in the same month are not statistically lower than the prior month's average (t-test p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS does not exceed 4.25% for at least 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in CPIAUCSL exceeds +2.5% in a month, it signals accelerating inflation expectations that compress real equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day rolling forward returns over the 60-day window are not statistically negative (t-test p > 0.05), or ΔCPIAUCSL ≤ +2.5% for the next 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden surge in PAYEMS (labor market additions) accompanied by a concurrent decline in UNRATE (unemployment) suggests a tight labor market that raises wage growth expectations and supports equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% in a month and UNRATE falls by >0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (Rank IC < 0.05) in the month of the signal, or the interaction index (Pearson/Spearman) < 0.3 for the 20-day window.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in GDPC1 (real private consumption) of at least 3% indicates weakening demand momentum, which lowers growth expectations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 decreases by ≥3% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day rolling forward returns over the 60-day horizon are not statistically negative (t-test p > 0.05), or GDPC1 recovers by ≥3% in the following month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in INDPRO (industrial production index) below 100 over a month signals supply-side weakness that reduces corporate earnings expectations and yields negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls below 100 in a month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in the following month are not statistically lower than the prior month's average (t-test p > 0.05), or INDPRO recovers to ≥100 within 2 months.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 1% for three consecutive months during a non-expansionary policy regime, it stabilizes discount rates and supports equity valuation resilience, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% for 3 consecutive months and regime_hint is not 'expansionary'
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the prior 20-day average (t-test p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS rises above 1% in the next month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in HOUST (housing starts) exceeding 1.5% month-over-month for two consecutive months, combined with UNRATE below 4%, indicates a housing recovery that boosts consumer confidence and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >1.5% in two consecutive months and UNRATE < 4%
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in the signal month are not statistically positive (Rank IC < 0.1), or the interaction index (Spearman) is negative.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in RSAFS (retail sales) of at least 4% for three months indicates deteriorating consumer demand, which lowers earnings expectations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases by ≥4% in three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day rolling forward returns over the 60-day window are not statistically negative (t-test p > 0.05), or RSAFS recovers by ≥4% within the next month.
